questions.q: What does a Terraform workspace provide?
options: A separate copy of the .tf configuration files
An isolated state file that the same configuration can be run against
A separate Terraform CLI installation
A dedicated cloud subscription
questions.explain: Workspaces let identical .tf files be applied against multiple separate state files, switched with a command, without duplicating the configuration itself.

questions.q: What workspace does every new Terraform configuration start in?
options: prod
dev
default
none — a workspace must be created manually before any command works
questions.explain: Terraform automatically creates and starts in a workspace named 'default' for every configuration.

questions.q: What does the terraform.workspace expression return?
options: The name of the current provider
The name of the currently selected workspace, usable inside configuration
The path to the state file
The Terraform CLI version
questions.explain: terraform.workspace returns the current workspace's name as a string, which can be interpolated into resource names or other values.

questions.q: Why did Northbridge Retail's platform team choose directory-per-environment over workspaces for production?
options: Workspaces are not supported by the azurerm or aws providers
Workspaces share the same files, variable defaults, and provider config, making it easy to accidentally target the wrong environment
Directory-per-environment does not require a backend
Workspaces cannot store state remotely
questions.explain: Because workspaces share the same configuration, a mistaken workspace selection can apply changes intended for one environment to another. Separate directories with separate backends make that mistake much harder to make.

questions.q: In what scenario does the lesson say workspaces still earn their place?
options: Managing production database credentials
Short-lived, low-risk scenarios like a feature-branch or pull-request preview environment
Replacing remote state entirely
Running Terraform without any provider configured
questions.explain: Workspaces' convenience of switching environments with one command fits throwaway, low-risk environments better than it fits production.
